# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 17 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 17 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_017_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 9

**1** After she had finished all this she said to me, "Do you want to see anything else?" Desiring to see more, I was overjoyed and said, "Lady, I would very much like to see." **2** She laughed and said, "Do you see seven women around the tower?" "I see them, lady," I said. "This tower," she said, "is being supported by these seven women. **3** The first, who grips it with her hands, is called Faith. Through her God's elect are saved. **4** The second, who is dressed in a long garment and is exceedingly beautiful, is called Continence. She is the daughter of Faith. Whoever follows her will be blessed in their life, because they abstain from all evil deeds, believing that if they abstain from all evil desire they will inherit eternal life." **5** "And the others, lady — who are they?" "They are daughters of one another in succession. The first is Faith; the second Continence; the third Simplicity; the fourth Knowledge; the fifth Innocence; the sixth Reverence; the seventh Agape." **6** "And what role do they have in the life of the believers?" "Listen," she said. "The one who follows these women and is able to hold fast to their works will dwell in the tower together with the saints of God. **7** And why are they called the daughters of one another? Because Continence is born from Faith; Simplicity is born from Continence; from Simplicity is born Innocence; from Innocence is born Reverence; from Reverence is born Knowledge; and from Knowledge is born Agape. Their works therefore are pure and reverent and divine."

---

*EMET note: Vision 3.9 gives the full theological lineage of the seven virtues: Faith → Continence → Simplicity → Innocence → Reverence → Knowledge → Agape. The chain is a virtue genealogy unique in early Christian literature.*
